PMID:42732304.topic: Distal radius fracture time to fixation
PMID:42732304.setting: Lincoln County Hospital, United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust; retrospective service evaluation of adult distal radius ORIF
PMID:42732304.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture standards: unstable intra-articular fractures fixed within 72 hours of injury; extra-articular fractures within seven days; re-displaced fractures within 72 hours of decision to operate

cycle1.result: Overall BOAST timing compliance 12% (3/25); extra-articular 100% (2/2), intra-articular 4.3% (1/23). Virtual fracture clinic pathway 0% (0/17) vs traditional trauma meeting 37.5% (3/8) (Fisher's exact p = 0.0243; OR 0.045, 95% CI 0.002-0.93).

PMID:42732304.other_findings: 94% (16/17) of virtual fracture clinic patients had a face-to-face clinic review before listing vs 0% (0/8) via the trauma meeting. Authors propose a direct-listing escalation protocol from virtual fracture clinic and a re-audit with timestamps at each pathway step.

PMID:39308745.setting: Major Trauma Centre for the South East of England, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust, Brighton; orthoplastic service
PMID:39308745.standard: BOAST 4 open lower limb fracture standards, e.g. IV antibiotics within 1 h of injury; debridement within 12 h for high-energy and 24 h for other fractures; definitive soft tissue cover within 72 h; gentamicin on induction; photographs; saline lavage

cycle1.result: Debridement within 24 h 81% (108/133); high-energy within 12 h 25% (15/60); mean time to first debridement 18.77 h. Definitive fixation/closure within 72 h 75% (95). Prehospital antibiotics within 1 h 76% (87/115); neurovascular documentation 94% (120/128); realignment and splinting 51% (45/89); photographs 86% (115); gentamicin on induction 65% (87); saline wash documented 78% (104).

PMID:39308745.other_findings: Post-operative infection rate 13% (16 patients); prehospital antibiotics within 1 h associated with lower infection (p<0.001). Documentation of prehospital care and intraoperative steps was frequently missing; authors recommend referral and operation note proformas and training.

PMID:33326412.topic: Bone health and secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture
PMID:33326412.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic department, University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire (major trauma centre)
PMID:33326412.standard: UHCW trust guidelines (in line with NICE) for secondary fragility fracture prevention: vitamin D/calcium supplementation, bone-sparing medication, DEXA scan for eligible patients, bone blood tests including PTH

cycle1.dates: Patients admitted immediately before the UK lockdown of 23 March 2020 (study period February to June 2020)
cycle1.result: Pre-lockdown baseline: orthogeriatric review 88% (44/50); vitamin D/calcium 40/49 (81.6%); bone-sparing medication 17/28 (60.7%); DEXA requested 9/22 (40.1%); PTH measured 5 (10%). Post-lockdown (n=50, before intervention): orthogeriatric review 0%; vitamin D/calcium 29/50 (58.0%, P=.02); bone-sparing medication 4/22 (18.2%, P=.004); DEXA 1/28 (3.6%, P=.003).

PMID:33326412.intervention: Audit results presented at the monthly T&O quality improvement meeting and the 'MRS BAD BONES' mnemonic disseminated to junior doctors, advanced nurse practitioners and medical students

cycle2.dates: After dissemination of the mnemonic (within February to June 2020)
cycle2.result: Vitamin D/calcium 42/49 (85.7%, P=.003 vs post-lockdown); bone-sparing medication 21/29 (72.4%, P<.001); DEXA requested 12/21 (60.0%, P<.001); orthogeriatric review 38% (19/50).

PMID:33326412.other_findings: PTH was measured in no patients after lockdown or after the intervention. The return of the orthogeriatric team during the post-intervention phase is a confounder.

PMID:26172938.topic: National hip fracture audit impact on care and mortality
PMID:26172938.setting: All NHS hospitals in England; national evaluation using Hospital Episode Statistics linked to ONS mortality data
PMID:26172938.standard: BOA/BGS six national hip fracture standards (including surgery within 48 hours); outcome measures were early surgery (day of or day after admission) and 30-day mortality

cycle1.result: Whole 2003-2011 cohort n=471,590. Before NHFD: early surgery fairly stable (annual RR 0.987, 1.3% relative decrease per year); 30-day mortality fell from 11.5% to 10.9% (1.8% relative reduction per year).

PMID:26172938.intervention: Launch of the National Hip Fracture Database in 2007: national clinical standards, continuous web-based audit feedback, helpline, website and regional meetings

cycle2.result: Early surgery rose from 54.5% to 71.3% (annual RR 1.080); 30-day mortality fell from 10.9% to 8.5% (7.6% relative reduction per year; P<0.001 for difference in trend).

PMID:26172938.other_findings: Hospitals submitting NHFD data rose from 11 in 2007 to all 175 by 2011. Best Practice Tariff from 2010 may have contributed to the rise in early surgery.

PMID:22416154.setting: Trauma centre, Government General Hospital (Indira Gandhi Government General Hospital), Puducherry; general surgery trauma ward

cycle1.result: 204 fatal cases: road traffic injuries caused 82% of deaths; 16% under the influence of alcohol; mean delay from injury to admission 14.9 hours (median 2.5 hours); 56% had at least one halt at another facility; head injury the commonest cause of death (66%); missed injuries at post mortem in 8%; only 21% (43/204) arrived within the golden hour.

PMID:22416154.other_findings: Missed injuries mostly involved the cervical spine and chest wall, and all missed cervical spine injuries were in alcohol-positive patients. None of the two-wheeler riders wore helmets.

PMID:37383496.topic: Surgical site infection after spinal surgery abroad
PMID:37383496.setting: Department of Orthopaedics (spine service), Khoula Hospital, Muscat; tertiary referral centre; patients who had spine surgery in India
PMID:37383496.standard: not reported (compared with Khoula Hospital's own spine surgery SSI rate of about 2.7% over the same period)

cycle1.result: SSI 12% (15/125) vs 2.7% (49/1833) for local spine surgery; 10 of 15 needed surgical debridement. Four neurological deteriorations, including 2 wrong-level surgeries.

PMID:37383496.other_findings: Of 80 patients seen locally before travel, 54 had been advised surgery; 42 of the 54 improved, while 14 of 19 patients not relieved had been advised against surgery. Fewer than half had complete documentation from the operating institution.

PMID:37783518.topic: Hip fracture early mobilisation by day after surgery
PMID:37783518.setting: 35-bed trauma ward, James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (district general hospital), Great Yarmouth
PMID:37783518.standard: NHFD metric: patient mobilised (standing or hoisted) out of bed by the day after surgery; target at least the UK national average of 81%

cycle1.dates: 6 months before the intervention (2019/2020, NHFD data); Hip Sprint audit September and December 2019
cycle1.result: Mean 60% of patients mobilised by the day after surgery. Hip Sprint cohort (n=60): 1.7% mobilised by healthcare assistants before physiotherapy assessment.

PMID:37783518.intervention: Therapy-led ward education programme for trauma healthcare assistants (1-hour 2:1 face-to-face session plus observed sign-off), ward posters and Trust media campaign, delivered over two PDSA cycles (June-July 2020 and June-August 2022)

cycle2.result: Mean 79.2% mobilised by the day after surgery after PDSA cycle 2 (from 60% in 2019). Healthcare assistant mobilisation before physiotherapy assessment 30% (n=51 cohort).

PMID:37783518.other_findings: After PDSA cycle 1 the rate rose to a mean of 78% but fell back to 71.8% in 2021, attributed to staff turnover. 30-day mortality fell from 10.1% to 7% between 2019 and 2022 (causality not established).

PMID:33083152.topic: Ottawa ankle and foot rules compliance for X-ray requests
PMID:33083152.setting: Emergency department, Flinders Medical Centre (tertiary hospital), South Australia
PMID:33083152.standard: Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria documented on adult ankle X-ray referrals

cycle1.result: 163/262 referrals met Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria; 99 of 262 (38%) did not. Compliance by profession: physiotherapists 77.3%, nurses 65.4%, consultants 61.5%, registrars/MOs/interns 54.8%. Overall sensitivity 0.59 and specificity 0.37.

PMID:33083152.other_findings: Registrars/MOs/interns were 2.5 times more likely than physiotherapists to refer despite not meeting the rules (OR 2.48, p = 0.026). Duration of injury was not specified on 76.3% of referrals.

PMID:38584819.topic: Female representation in fifth metatarsal fracture research
PMID:38584819.setting: Literature audit of PubMed-indexed studies, University of Kansas

cycle1.result: Of 472 fifth metatarsal fractures, 373 (79%) were in males and 99 (21%) in females. Studies: 18 mixed cohort (60%), 10 male only (33.33%), 1 female only (3.33%), 1 male vs female (3.33%); mixed cohorts 605/831 (72.8%) male.

PMID:38584819.other_findings: Only the single female-only study accounted for menstrual status, and no study investigated female performance. No study reported outcomes by sex.

PMID:40575204.topic: Ottawa ankle and foot rules compliance for X-ray requests
PMID:40575204.setting: Emergency department, South London district general hospital
PMID:40575204.standard: ED clerking documentation and X-ray request clinical details should contain the relevant Ottawa Ankle or Foot Rule criteria in all cases (NICE; RCR/IR(ME)R 2017)

cycle1.result: 100 ankle and 100 foot X-ray requests. Ankle: documentation compliance 74%, X-ray request compliance 43%. Foot: documentation compliance 48%, X-ray request compliance 32%.

PMID:40575204.intervention: First-cycle results distributed and an Ottawa rules handout given to ED staff, plus a small-group teaching session for ED junior doctors on assessing, documenting and requesting foot and ankle X-rays (mid-April 2024)

cycle2.result: Ankle: documentation 87% (p<.05), X-ray request 57% (p<.05). Foot: documentation 78% (p<.001 in abstract; p<.0001 in results), X-ray request 54% (p<.01).

PMID:40575204.other_findings: Ankle fracture rate rose from 17% to 22% (p=.37) and midfoot fracture rate stayed at 15%. Foot compliance stayed lower than ankle compliance in both cycles; authors suggest an electronic X-ray request template.
